title: The Confluence Of Risks
gist: Gavekal's Louis-Vincent Gave says several tail risks materialized last week and that, with US midterms near, the Trump administration is losing its ability to hold energy prices down amid low inventories and wars.

insights.claim: Several tail risks flagged in an earlier Gavekal piece began to materialize in earnest last week.
insights.speaker: Louis-Vincent Gave
insights.so_what: Raises the risk of a broader market shake-out.

insights.claim: With midterms around the corner, the Trump administration's ability to keep energy prices down is rapidly disappearing.
insights.speaker: Louis-Vincent Gave
insights.so_what: Political pressure on energy prices may drive policy interventions and volatility.

insights.claim: Near-term energy prices are highly uncertain because inventories are low or non-existent, wars in Russia/Ukraine and the Middle East continue, ships are scarce, refineries and pipelines are being destroyed, and Black Sea, Red Sea and Persian Gulf sea lanes are not entirely safe.
insights.speaker: Louis-Vincent Gave
insights.so_what: Thin inventories mean supply shocks transmit sharply to prices; hold energy-supply hedges.
